Pneumocystis pneumonia Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) is caused by the organism Pneumocystis jirovecii (previously named Pneumocystis carinii f. sp. hominis and at one time considered to be a protozoan). It is an opportunistic pathogen and infection is acquired by inhalation. In persons with normally function- ing immune systems infection rarely produces disease, but in immunocompromised patients it may produce intersti- tial pneumonia which, if untreated, is almost always fatal. In patients with AIDS (p.856), Pneumocystis pneumonia is a common occurrence. The treatment of choice for PCP is: • intravenous or oral co-trimoxazole1-4 Alternative regimens are:1-4 • intravenous pentamidine • oral clindamycin and primaquine • oral atovaquone • oral trimethoprim and dapsone • nebulised pentamidine is occasionally suggested for mild to moderate infection but is now generally reserved for prophylax- is. • intravenous trimetrexate plus folinic acid may be a further op- tion to intravenous co-trimoxazole or pentamidine in patients with moderate to severe disease.
